- Output: `/home/mara/cwe-bench/sibling2/out/screener/33021.json`. I checked the cited lines against the pinned tree, except the showconfig and graphs line numbers.
- Trust decision: strings that come from devices (SNMP fields, syslog program/date, Oxidized data, stored alert details) are trusted and printed as raw HTML. Each echo site in `includes/html/*` decides on its own whether to escape. The fix wraps 16 files in `e()`.
- `pattern_fit`: A+B. Pattern A: the alert-details renderer reads compressed JSON from `alert_log` (`includes/html/functions.inc.php:457-653`), which a solver can dismiss as internal data. Pattern B: about 11 unfixed routes, including exact copies of the fixed sensor code in `includes/html/pages/device/port/sensors.inc.php:13-23` and `includes/html/pages/device/wireless.inc.php:81-96`.
- Strongest lever: two problems a careful solver must actually understand. In tooltip popups, `e()` sits inside a JS string in an `onmouseover` attribute, so the browser decodes the escaped quote before the JS runs (`includes/html/pages/device/health/storage.inc.php:27`); I worked this out from reading and didn't run it. And in `includes/html/pages/device/slas.inc.php:110-124`, one branch wraps the SLA name in a link and leaves it raw while the other escapes it.
- Biggest red flag: none of the defined flags apply. The real concerns are that most extra routes are the same idea in more places, which models tend to fix together. Also, the published fix itself adds a debug `<script>alert("hello")</script>` line to the sensor name (`fix.diff:129`), so it must not go into the reference solution.
